transcript.content: Hello! Welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Thank you for seeing me. Lately I keep thinking my clients would be better off if I just weren’t here, and those thoughts about not wanting to wake up are starting to really scare me.
I'm so sorry you're feeling this way, and I'm glad you came in. Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change in your life recently?

Yeah, they started about a month ago after a really stressful stretch at work. I had a cluster of difficult cases and then a tense disagreement with my supervising clinician about treatment plans, which just left me feeling completely incompetent and out of my depth.
Have you ever experienced periods of feeling this low or depressed in the past, or is this the first time you've felt this way?
No, this is definitely the first time I've ever felt this way. I don't recall ever experiencing periods of depression or feeling this low in the past.
Have you also noticed a significant loss of interest or pleasure in the activities and hobbies you normally enjoy?

Yes, definitely. I used to really look forward to my guitar jams and hanging out with friends after work, but lately it all just feels completely pointless. I'd honestly rather just sit in the dark staring at nothing than pretend I'm enjoying myself.
Along with these feelings, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your energy levels over the past month?

My sleep is awful; I lie in bed exhausted but wired, waking up multiple times a night and getting up at 5 a.m. feeling completely unrefreshed. On top of that, my energy is totally gone, and even simple things like showering or walking to the clinic feel like I've run a marathon.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight, or have you been having trouble concentrating and making decisions lately?

Yes, both have been a struggle. I have no appetite and have to force myself to eat, so my pants are looser and coworkers have been asking if I'm losing weight. My brain also feels like mud—I lose my train of thought mid-sentence and get completely paralyzed by simple decisions like what to eat or writing a short progress note.
Have these feelings of low mood, exhaustion, and loss of interest been present nearly every day, for most of the day, over this past month?

Yes, absolutely. Ever since that stressful stretch at the clinic about a month ago, these feelings have been there pretty much every single day, all day long. It feels like there is just no break from it.
To help me rule out other potential causes, do you have any medical conditions like thyroid issues, or are you currently taking any medications or using substances?
No, I don't have any medical conditions like thyroid issues that I know of. I'm also not currently taking any medications or using any substances.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-time depressive episode characterized by depressed mood, loss of interest/pleasure, marked fatigue, insomnia, decreased appetite with weight loss, impaired concentration, feelings of worthlessness, and suicidal ideation (not wanting to wake up). These symptoms have been present daily for approximately one month and cause significant functional impairment. Although the episode was preceded by a work-related stressor, the severity, number, and persistence of symptoms meet the full criteria for a major depressive episode (F32), which supersedes a diagnosis of adjustment disorder (F43.2).
